notes.note: List plus length subtype of a record of is allowed by the SubTypeSpec BNF but forbidden by 6.2.13.4; Titan does not implement this check (accepts).

Ambiguous consequence; the only way to hand a timer reference to another component instance is via parameters of a started function, which 5.4.1.1 l) forbids statically, so a reject test is used. Neither runtime reading (dynamic error / unspecified) can be constructed in valid TTCN-3.
Titan does not support timer-typed variables fully and parses v_copy.running as component running; test is correct per 6.2.14 / 11.1 example (var timer).
Uses MapType.from / value.from (6.2.15.5) to observe the key type; Titan lacks map support (syntax error).
Uses MapType.to / value.to (6.2.15.6); Titan lacks map support (syntax error).

The trailing "," in the syntax box is read as a separator (as in the clause examples). All Titan warnings on map accept/reject tests in this batch (6.2.15.x) are due to missing map type support in Titan ([*] syntax, map restrictions not checked).
Ambiguity one-or-more vs zero-or-more assignments after *: test uses * followed by one assignment, valid under both readings.
Violation chosen: unmap(template, ?) i.e. a matching symbol other than the asterisk literal. Note that BNF rule 300 UnmapStatement lacks the "*" alternative given in clause 6.2.15.3.
Reading including template variables chosen; violation tested is a map constant as ValueRef (not a variable). Uninitialized variables would only be detectable at runtime.
Partial initialization of a key is generally only detectable at runtime, so the test expects a test case error (ttcn3verdict:error).
